faq.q1: What is AI Real Estate Assistant?
faq.a1: An open-source conversational AI platform for property search, analytics, and market insights. Ask in natural language — for example "2-bedroom apartment in Kraków under 500k" — and get matched listings. Built with FastAPI, Next.js, and ChromaDB.
faq.q2: How is it different from Zillow, Rightmove, or Idealista?
faq.a2: It is AI-first and conversational rather than filter-first. The natural-language interface, hybrid semantic + keyword search, multi-provider LLM fallback chain, and self-hostable MIT-licensed stack make it a developer-friendly alternative for building custom property experiences.
faq.a3: Yes. MIT-licensed with Docker Compose, a 5-minute quickstart, and full source on GitHub. Add your own LLM API keys (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Grok, DeepSeek, or local Ollama) and ChromaDB-backed data.
faq.a4: The live demo uses simulated AI responses and curated mock data for instant exploration — no signup needed. A production deployment with real listings requires API keys and your own data source.
faq.q5: What is the difference from PropVector AI?
faq.a5: PropVector AI (propvectorai.com) is a hosted SaaS tier built on this open-source codebase, with managed accounts, live data feeds, AI CRM, and enterprise capabilities. The repository stays open-core: the engine remains free, while commercial features live in the hosted product.
faq.a6: 9 languages for the UI and chat: English, Polish, Russian, German, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese, Turkish, and Ukrainian. EU AI Act compliance labels are included.
faq.a7: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Grok, DeepSeek, and local Ollama. Automatic fallback chain ensures reliability. Provider selection is per-task and per-user with priority cascade.
faq.q8: Is there a hosted version with real data?
faq.a8: Yes — PropVector AI (propvectorai.com) offers hosted tiers with live data, managed accounts, and enterprise capabilities. The open-source repo stays focused on the core engine and a self-hostable demo experience.

features.body: Each line opens the part of the demo it describes. All six work without an account.

1.title: Natural-language search

data.title: Data and coverage, as of today.
data.body: The engine is not tied to a country. Listings you bring — a CSV or XLSX import, a registered data source, your own database — are searched, mapped and priced in their own currency, anywhere. The demo serves a seeded Polish catalogue, and the first live provider integration is Polish; the rest of the EU, the UK and the US are next in line.

limits.title: What the demo is, and what it is not.

1.title: A model we pay for
1.text: The demo answers with a hosted model and falls back to a local one if the hosted one is unreachable, so exploring costs nothing and needs no account.

2.title: Your own key
2.text: A real deployment uses the provider key you bring — any of 17 providers, or a local Ollama — and falls back to the next one when a provider fails.

3.title: Your own data
3.text: SQLite plus a ChromaDB index on a volume you own, in your country, behind your own authentication.

faq.title: Questions people actually ask.
faq.q1: Can I run it on my own server?
faq.a1: Yes — that is what the project is for. One compose file, or let this repository’s CI do it: give the self-host deploy workflow a key and an address as repository secrets, and every release tag rolls your machine onto the new images.
faq.q2: Do I need a paid API key?
faq.a2: Not to look around. The demo answers with a model we pay for, so it costs nothing to explore. For real answers you bring your own key — any of 17 providers, or a local Ollama — and the app falls back to the next one when a provider fails.
faq.q3: What is the difference to the hosted version?
faq.a3: The engine is the same. The hosted tier adds live data feeds, accounts, saved searches, alerts and an AI CRM — see PropVector AI.
faq.a4: Nine in the interface: English, Polish, Russian, German, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese, Turkish and Ukrainian. The documentation is English-first.
faq.a5: Yes, for anything you run yourself: SQLite plus a ChromaDB index on a volume you own, in your country, behind your own authentication.
faq.a6: MIT. Fork it, change it, ship it. The hosted version is the commercial path for teams that want the managed pieces instead of running the stack.
